newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Chevron bids to build West African gas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Chevron bids to build West African gas pipeline.

text.p: Chevron Corp is bidding to construct a pipeline to carry Nigerian gas to three West African countries, a Nigerian official said on Friday.

"The Chevron proposal to be private developer for the project will be considered at next month's steering committee meeting on October 14 in Ghana," Akin Okubote, special assistant to Nigerian Oil Minister Dan Etete, told Reuters.
Okubote said Nigeria favoured handing the project to a private developer. But he did not say if Nigeria was backing the Chevron bid.
"Putting it in private hands would remove bureaucracy and ensure maximum returns," he said.
The four countries involved -- Nigeria, Benin, Togo and Ghana -- had initially proposed to set up a West African Gas Pipeline Company to manage the project.
After an eight-month delay an agreement to implement the project was signed in July.
The pipeline would carry gas from Chevron's Escravos field which is currently being flared.
According to a World Bank study, West African nations would benefit from cheap and plentiful Nigerian gas if the project estimated at about $260 million is successfully implemented.
